ordered_diagnoses: Multiple Hereditary Infundibulocystic Basal Cell Carcinomas

s1.syndrome_frame: Multiple skin-colored papules on the face and vulva with a gradual increase in number over time
salient_findings: Multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored papules on the face and vulva
Lesions first appeared around 50 years of age and gradually increased
Family history of similar facial papules
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 60s
Multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored papules are present on the face and vulva
Lesions first appeared around 50 years of age
Lesions gradually increased to approximately 60
Patient has a medical history of meningioma
Family history is notable for a daughter with similar facial papules
No palmar or plantar pits were observed
Histopathology showed buds and cords of basaloid cells enclosing small cystic spaces
Clefting between tumor aggregates and the surrounding stroma was focally evident
Whole-exome sequencing revealed a conserved splice-site mutation in the SUFU gene

shortlist.label: Nevoid Basal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored papules and a medical history of meningioma, which are characteristic features of this syndrome

shortlist.label: Gorlin Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to Nevoid Basal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome, this condition also presents with multiple basal cell carcinomas and other characteristic features such as palmar or plantar pits, although none were observed in this case

shortlist.label: Infundibulocystic Basal Cell Carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathology showed buds and cords of basaloid cells enclosing small cystic spaces, consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Generalized Basaloid Follicular Hamartoma Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has multiple skin-colored papules and a family history of similar lesions, which could be indicative of this rare condition

shortlist.label: Multiple Hereditary Infundibulocystic Basal Cell Carcinomas
shortlist.why_kept: Whole-exome sequencing revealed a conserved splice-site mutation in the SUFU gene, which is associated with this condition

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of multiple dome-shaped, skin-colored papules on the face and vulva, along with a history of meningioma and a family history of similar lesions, combined with the histopathological findings and the genetic mutation in the SUFU gene, are all consistent with Nevoid Basal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome (Gorlin Syndrome). The presence of a conserved splice-site mutation in the SUFU gene, which is a known cause of Gorlin Syndrome, further supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Gorlin Syndrome
rejected.why: Gorlin Syndrome is another name for Nevoid Basal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome, so it is not a distinct alternative

rejected.label: Infundibulocystic Basal Cell Carcinoma
rejected.why: While the histopathology shows features of infundibulocystic basal cell carcinoma, the overall clinical presentation and genetic findings are more consistent with Nevoid Basal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome

rejected.label: Generalized Basaloid Follicular Hamartoma Syndrome
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with a different set of clinical and histopathological features, and is not associated with the same genetic mutations

rejected.label: Multiple Hereditary Infundibulocystic Basal Cell Carcinomas
rejected.why: This condition is not a recognized syndrome, and the patient's presentation is more consistent with Nevoid Basal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome

gold: Multiple hereditary infundibulocystic basal cell carcinoma syndrome (MHIBCC)
